title: Launch and open a project
description: Forge PHP is a standalone PHP and CodeIgniter workspace with its own local PHP runtime.
steps: Double-click the Forge PHP shortcut on your Desktop.
Use File > Open Folder to open the folder containing composer.json and, for CodeIgniter, spark.
Trust the folder only if you trust its PHP code and Composer scripts.
Choose Forge: Configure Project to add tasks and Xdebug launch settings without replacing existing named entries.
note: Keep the Desktop IDE folder in place for the existing shortcut. The development build and packaged releases have separate settings locations.

title: Create a CodeIgniter application
description: Create an application using Composer and the official CodeIgniter appstarter.
steps: Open Project > New CodeIgniter Project, or run the command below.
Choose a parent directory and a new folder name.
Wait for Composer to finish. Forge adds development settings and opens the project.
note: Internet access is required. Existing folders are preserved.

title: PHP intelligence and navigation
description: Intelephense provides PHP highlighting, suggestions, signatures, diagnostics and navigation.
steps: Open a PHP file and wait for project indexing.
Type a member expression such as $object-> to get suggestions; Ctrl+Space requests them manually.
Use F12 for definition, Shift+F12 for references and Ctrl+P to find files.
Review diagnostics in the Problems panel.
note: Some Intelephense refactoring features require your own paid licence. Composer dependencies improve type information.

title: CodeIgniter completions and related views
description: Suggest project model/config names, services, language keys, validation rules, view paths and .env keys.
steps: Type model(' , config(' , service(' , lang(' or view(' and request completion.
For rules, use a quoted 'rules' => '...' value; suggestions also appear after a pipe.
Open .env and request completion before the equals sign.
Use Forge: Related View to navigate from view(), extend() or include() calls.
note: This is static source discovery. Dynamic PHP arrays, nested language keys, custom namespace mappings and every possible validation syntax are not fully resolved.

title: Formatting on save
description: Use the project's PHP coding standard when configured; otherwise use bundled Prettier. Prettier also formats JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, HTML, CSS, Markdown and YAML.
steps: Install the project's Composer development dependencies.
Put .php-cs-fixer.php/.php-cs-fixer.dist.php or phpcs.xml/.phpcs.xml (including .dist variants) at the workspace root.
Save a PHP file. Forge runs vendor/bin/php-cs-fixer or vendor/bin/phpcbf with that configuration.
By default, only formatting hunks wholly inside lines changed since Git HEAD are applied. Without Git history, the saved disk version is the baseline.
Set forge.formatChangedLinesOnly to false if you explicitly want whole-file project formatting.
note: A configured but missing or failed formatter does not silently fall back to Prettier. Hunks crossing unchanged lines are skipped. PHP-CS-Fixer uses a temporary sibling file, so filename-specific rules may behave differently. Prettier fallback still formats the whole file.

title: Multiple monitors and split editors
description: Keep different files open in separate editor windows, sharing the same project session.
steps: Open the files you need.
Drag an editor tab outside the main window, or focus it and press Ctrl+Alt+O.
Move the detached window to your other display.
Use Forge > Bring All Editors Back to restore detached editors.
For an in-window split, use the editor tab's context menu or split-editor control.
note: Keep the main window open while using detached editors.

title: Bookmarks and local history
description: Bookmark useful locations and compare previous saved file versions.
steps: Press Ctrl+Alt+B to toggle the current file/line bookmark.
Press Ctrl+Alt+J to choose a bookmark.
Save files normally to collect local snapshots, or use Save Local Snapshot.
Press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+H and choose a version to compare with the current file.
note: History keeps 20 versions per supported file up to 512 KB, across 500 recent files. It is not a backup. Bookmarks store line numbers and can move out of date after large edits.

title: Development server and HTTP connection errors
description: Run CodeIgniter with the bundled PHP runtime.
steps: Select CodeIgniter · Development in the top toolbar and click Run, or press Shift+F10.
Use Open Local Site to launch the site.
Use localhost in request URLs to match the server's binding; it may resolve to IPv6 on Windows.
If a request is refused, check the server terminal and the URL's host and port.
Press Shift+F2 or click Stop to stop a Forge-managed server.
note: The default port is 8080. Configure forge.serverPort if needed. A missing route returns 404; it is different from a refused connection.

title: Xdebug debugging
description: Launch PHP under Xdebug and inspect stack frames, variables and breakpoints.
steps: Configure the project, then click beside a PHP line number to add a breakpoint.
Press Shift+F9 or click Debug to start the CodeIgniter debug configuration.
Make a browser or HTTP request to execute the breakpoint.
Use the Debug pane to step through code and inspect values.
Choose Debug Current PHP File, Debug PHPUnit or Listen for Xdebug from the Run/Debug configuration list when needed.
note: External servers, Docker and remote interpreters need their own Xdebug paths and connection configuration.

title: Terminal, Composer and Spark
description: Run project tools in the integrated terminal with the bundled PHP available on PATH.
steps: Click Terminal at the bottom or use Forge: Project Terminal.
Use Forge: Composer to install/update/audit dependencies or run a Composer script.
Use Forge: Run Spark Command to choose commands discovered from your application.
Supply Spark arguments as a JSON array, for example ["Users","--suffix"].
note: The terminal is unrestricted: commands you type there do not pass through Forge's database confirmation checks.

title: Class generation and route inspection
description: Generate framework classes and explore resolved application routes.
steps: Use Generate Class, choose a type and enter a PascalCase name.
Open Route Inspector to search resolved routes by path, method or controller.
Click a controller handler to jump to its method.
Save app/Config/Routes.php while the inspector is open to refresh it.
Place the caret inside a controller method, then right-click > Forge: Find Routes for Controller Method.
Click Create HTTP request on a route to append a request to an open requests.http document, or create requests.http if none exists.
note: Replace generated route parameters before sending. Generated routes or routes in included files may not have a direct source location. Route discovery executes the trusted application's Spark router.

title: REST requests and API testing
description: Write and run API calls from .http files with the bundled REST Client.
steps: Use HTTP Client to open requests.http.
Write a request such as GET http://localhost:8080/ followed by headers.
Separate requests with ###. Use @baseUrl = http://localhost:8080 and {{baseUrl}} for variables.
For JSON, add Content-Type: application/json, a blank line, then the JSON body.
Click Send Request above a request or press Ctrl+Alt+Enter.
Inspect the status, headers and body in the response view.
note: Request files can contain credentials. Use environment variables and keep secrets out of Git. Generated requests are never sent automatically.

title: PHPStan with CodeIgniter support
description: Find type and application errors beyond PHP syntax checking.
steps: Run Forge: Set Up PHPStan + CodeIgniter to install project development dependencies.
New projects get a level-6 phpstan.neon including the official CodeIgniter extension and test bootstrap.
If a config already exists, add the extension include yourself; Forge preserves it.
Run Forge: Analyze with PHPStan. Saved source is analyzed and findings appear in Problems and the PHPStan output channel.
note: Analysis is manual. The CodeIgniter extension boots application configuration and may execute migrations against temporary SQLite for schema inference. Only analyze trusted projects; testing environment does not guarantee custom bootstrap code is side-effect free.

title: Tests, linting and quality checks
description: Run application PHPUnit tests, PHP syntax checks, Composer validation and dependency auditing.
steps: Use Run Tests for the complete project suite or Run Current Test for an open PHP test file.
Use PHP Syntax Check to lint the current PHP file.
Use Quality Checks for Composer validation, audit, PHPUnit and application/test syntax checks.
Run PHPStan separately for static analysis.
note: The IDE's own source checks are separate: run npm test and npm run lint at the IDE repository root.

title: Environment visibility and database writes
description: The status bar displays CI_ENVIRONMENT and the default database host from .env.
steps: Edit .env; the status refreshes after save.
Click the environment status to open .env.
When using Forge's migrate, migrate:* or db:seed commands, review the project, command and displayed database values.
Confirm the first dialog, then type the requested project/host phrase to authorize the write.
note: Both checks apply even to local databases. .env is not proof of the runtime target: PHP config, process variables and command flags can override it. Terminal commands, user-authored tasks and Composer scripts are outside this guard.

title: SQLTools connection from .env
description: Load MySQLi or PostgreSQL connection metadata without copying a password into settings.
steps: Set database.default.hostname, database, username, DBDriver and port in .env.
Run Forge: Load SQLTools Connection from .env.
Open the resulting Forge connection in the SQLTools sidebar.
Enter the password when prompted. Query and browse using SQLTools.
Re-run the importer after changing connection details.
note: Passwords are prompted, not imported from .env. Existing manually saved profiles are not rewritten. SQLite, DSNs, SSH tunnels and custom database groups require manual configuration.

title: Git and source control
description: Review changes, stage files, commit and compare revisions through the Source Control pane.
steps: Open a Git repository, or initialize one using Git in the terminal.
Open View > Source Control to review the changes.
Inspect diffs before staging and committing.
Use Git commands in the terminal for advanced workflows.
note: Forge's own source is also now in a local Git repository. Runtime data, user projects, dependencies and secrets are ignored. No remote repository has been created.

title: Themes, settings and logs
description: Choose a workspace appearance, configure tools and inspect application logs.
steps: Click Theme and choose Graphite, Abyss, Orchid or Paper.
Use Settings to change font, formatter, server port and PHP paths.
Use Application Logs to follow the latest CodeIgniter writable/logs file.
Use Toolchain Diagnostics to inspect PHP extensions, Composer, Git and installed integrations.

title: Built-in PHP and CodeIgniter documentation
description: Search and read official reference articles inside Forge.
steps: Click Documentation and choose a PHP or CodeIgniter topic.
Use Shift+F1 from PHP to look up the current function.
Follow supported documentation links inside the reader.
Previously cached articles remain available offline.
note: The cache is a selection of reference pages, not a complete offline copy of both websites.

title: Gemma and Google Gemini
description: Choose between local Gemma 4 E4B and Google Gemini in the right sidebar. Both stream replies.
steps: Open Gemma Assistant with Ctrl+Alt+A and enable it.
Install the standalone llmster runtime and a Gemma 4 E4B model. Use Start runtime if the local server is off.
Choose Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite for quicker replies or Gemini 3.5 Flash for more reasoning. Use Set Gemini API key to save or replace its key.
Leave project lookups enabled to send an excerpt from the active editor, including unsaved edits, and let Gemini request more project files as needed.
Expand Thinking summary and file lookups to see summaries Google provides and which paths Gemini opened.
Attach a selection or file to include code in the next request.
Send a question. Use Stop to cancel, or Copy and Insert on a completed code block.
note: Gemma stays on this PC. Gemini sends the current conversation, attachments and selected project context to Google. Disable project lookups to omit automatic project context. File access is read-only, capped per turn, and excludes common credential files, dependency folders and binaries. Google may omit thinking summaries, especially in fast mode. Switching models keeps the transcript and carries recent turns into your next request. Switching to Gemini shares those turns with Google when you send. Use New chat to start without prior context.

title: Forge Git commit graph
description: Browse the branch and merge history, open diffs, and run Git and GitHub actions.
steps: Open the project folder, then open Forge Git with Ctrl+Alt+G. Choose Initialize repository if the folder is new to Git.
Save your files with Ctrl+S. Open Changes and use + next to each file you want to include. Check that your .gitignore excludes secrets and generated files.
Return to Forge Git and choose Commit staged. Enter a message and, if prompted, a commit name and email.
Choose Sign in to GitHub and complete the browser authorization. Use Publish to GitHub for a new remote, or GitHub → Set GitHub remote and Push for an existing one.
Click any commit to inspect its patch. Use Actions for branches, merges, rebases, stashes, and tags.
note: GitHub actions use GitHub CLI and your own account permissions. Use Changes for file-by-file staging.
